rationale: All three premises check out against the patch: the NaN-laden test input, the delegation chain mode->leadingValues->dominantEntries->mostFrequent->countEntries->tabulate, and tabulate adding every value with no isNaN guard (the removed filter). The chain's own third step places the first wrong state (NaN in the Frequency table) at tabulate, and nothing in the chain indicts mostFrequent: its reverse-index copy is faithful and its javadoc ('most frequently occurring values') is literally satisfied by [NaN] on the trigger input. Partly defensible only because the sub-method docs are silent on NaN.
